title: A torus-fixed point in a proper homogeneous space has a Borel stabilizer through that torus
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group scheme isomorphic to $(\mathbf G_m)^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$, with $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]; a maximal torus is a torus subgroup maximal under inclusion. A group is solvable if its successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]; a Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup. Let $G$ be smooth and connected, and let $Y$ be a nonempty smooth connected proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with an action $a:G\times_kY\to Y$ satisfying the unit and multiplication identities. Assume that $G(k)$ acts transitively on $Y(k)$. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a maximal torus, and let $y\in Y(k)$ be fixed scheme-theoretically by $T$, meaning that $a(t,y_A)=y_A$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $t\in T(A)$. There exists a Borel subgroup $B_0\subseteq G$ containing $T$ and fixing $y$ scheme-theoretically: for every such $A$ and every $b\in B_0(A)$, $a(b,y_A)=y_A$. No smoothness of the full scheme-theoretic stabilizer of $y$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 17.16 and its proof, printed p.356 (a complete orbit stabilizer contains a Borel); Theorem 17.10, printed pp.354--355 (conjugacy of maximal tori inside the reduced identity stabilizer); proof of Theorem 17.65, printed p.374, sentence asserting a Borel subgroup between T and the parabolic dual-line stabilizer.

proof.text: Choose a Borel subgroup $B$ of $G$ by [lem-sfb-borel-conjugation-cover]. Its restricted action on $Y$ has a scheme-theoretically fixed point $z\in Y(k)$ by [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point]: $B$ is smooth connected solvable and $Y$ is nonempty proper of finite type. Transitivity gives $g\in G(k)$ with $z=gy$. Put $C=g^{-1}Bg$. Conjugation is a group-scheme automorphism and preserves smoothness, connectedness, solvability and maximality, so $C$ is Borel. For every $k$-algebra $A$ and $c=g_A^{-1}bg_A\in C(A)$, $cy_A=g_A^{-1}bz_A=y_A$. Thus $C$ fixes $y$ scheme-theoretically.

source.place: Theorem 17.16, converse proof, printed p.356; Corollary 17.3, p.353; Definition 17.6, p.353.

proof.text: Let $H=G_y$ be the closed scheme-theoretic stabilizer supplied by [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. The preceding identity gives $C\subseteq H$ and the hypothesis gives $T\subseteq H$, both on all algebras. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], $K=(H^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a smooth connected finite-type group scheme. It is a closed subgroup of the affine group $G$, hence affine. No reducedness or smoothness of $H$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 17.10 and reduction to the identity component of the stabilizer; Stacks groupoids.tex Tags 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), 047R (lemma-reduced-subgroup-scheme-perfect), 047P (lemma-reduced-group-scheme-prefect-field-characteristic-p-smooth).

proof.text: Both $C$ and $T$ factor through $K$. Indeed $C$ is connected and is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] applied over $k$. For $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$, [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] with $L=\mathbf Z^r$ gives a domain coordinate ring $k[L]$, so $T$ is reduced and connected: the zero prime is a generic point, and every nonempty open contains it. The image of either connected group contains the identity and lies in the connected component $H^0$. Since $H^0$ is open, the morphism factors through that open subscheme. On affine opens every nilpotent section pulls back to zero on a reduced source; the quotient description in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] then gives factorization through $(H^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. These factorizations preserve the subgroup embeddings.

source.place: Theorem 17.10, printed pp.354--355, applied to the reduced identity stabilizer; elementary factorization through its open identity component and nilradical quotient.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy], the Borel $C$ contains a torus $S$ maximal in $G$. Both $S$ and $T$ are tori in $K$. Each is maximal in $K$, since any strictly larger torus in $K$ would also be a strictly larger torus in $G$. Apply the conjugacy clause of the same node to the smooth connected affine group $K$: there is $h\in K(k)$ with $hSh^{-1}=T$ as subgroup schemes.

source.place: Theorem 17.10 and paragraph following Definition 17.12, printed pp.354--355.

proof.text: Set $B_0=hCh^{-1}$. Conjugation preserves the Borel property, and $T=hSh^{-1}\subseteq B_0$. Since $h\in K(k)\subseteq H(k)$ fixes $y$, for any $k$-algebra $A$ and $b=h_Ach_A^{-1}\in B_0(A)$ the action identities give $by_A=h_Ac(h_A^{-1}y_A)=h_Acy_A=h_Ay_A=y_A$. This proves every asserted containment and fixed-point identity, including on nonreduced test algebras.
